Roughly two and a half hours after the initial 911 call, Grand Blanc Township firefighters extinguished the inferno. Two bodies were pulled from the rubble, while two other victims died on scene from gunshot wounds. 8 survivors were transported to nearby Henry Ford Genesis Hospital, 5 for gunshot wounds and 3 for smoke inhalation. The youngest victim, a 6-year-old child, was treated for a gunshot wound to the arm and released several days later. According to CNN, nurses and emergency personnel who were on strike at the nearby hospital left the picket line when they heard about the shooting to provide medical aid to the survivors. The shooter, a U.S. Marine who served in Fallujah Iraq, was pronounced dead at the scene. According to a childhood friend interviewed by the conversation, the shooter was also a longtime methamphetamine user, suggesting meth-induced psychosis as a contributing factor. The shooting was Michigan's second church shooting of 2025. Two months later, the church was demolished, and the congregation has plans to rebuild on the same site.
